criteria.criterion: The selected firmware target configuration identifies the NUCLEO-C5A3ZG board and its MB2310 reference.
criteria.observable: Board-target configuration entry
procedure: Inspect the firmware's selected board-target configuration.
Compare the board name and reference with the required target.
criteria.expected: The configuration identifies NUCLEO-C5A3ZG, reference MB2310.
criteria.rationale: The requirement specifies the board and reference, and its verification method is Inspection; checking the selected target configuration is a checkable way to establish which board the firmware targets.

criteria.criterion: The selected MCU target configuration names STM32C5A3ZGT6 and specifies the Cortex-M33 core.
criteria.observable: MCU target and processor-core configuration
procedure: Inspect the selected MCU target and processor configuration.
Compare the part number and core with the requirement.
criteria.expected: The target is STM32C5A3ZGT6 and the core is Cortex-M33.

criteria.criterion: The MCU part specification identifies single-precision FPU and DSP capability for STM32C5A3ZGT6.
criteria.observable: MCU part specification for STM32C5A3ZGT6
procedure: Inspect the specification for the selected MCU part.
Check its listed FPU precision and DSP capability.
criteria.expected: The specification lists a single-precision FPU and DSP capability.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's parameters name these MCU capabilities, but its stated acceptance criterion only names the MCU and core; the part specification provides an inspection observable for the additional constraints.

criteria.criterion: The configured maximum CPU clock does not exceed 144 MHz.
criteria.observable: Clock configuration's maximum CPU frequency
procedure: Inspect the selected clock configuration.
Read the configured maximum CPU clock.
criteria.expected: CPU clock is at most 144 MHz.

criteria.criterion: The linked firmware image occupies no more than 1 MiB of Flash.
criteria.observable: Linker map or equivalent image-size report
preconditions: The firmware image has been built.
procedure: Inspect the linker map or image-size report.
Read the total Flash image size.
criteria.expected: Flash image size is at most 1 MiB.

criteria.criterion: The linked firmware's SRAM usage does not exceed 256 KiB.
criteria.observable: Linker map or equivalent memory-usage report
preconditions: The firmware image has been built.
procedure: Inspect the linker map or memory-usage report.
Read the SRAM allocation, including static and reserved application sections reported there.
criteria.expected: Reported SRAM usage is at most 256 KiB.

criteria.criterion: The application's required dependency and startup configuration contains no mandatory external sensor, external memory, network service, RTOS, or NPU.
criteria.observable: Application dependency list and startup/configuration code
procedure: Inspect the application dependency list and startup/configuration path.
Check whether any listed component or service is required for the application to start and execute its test.
criteria.expected: None of the five listed components or services is a mandatory application dependency.

criteria.criterion: The selected board configuration names the UART instance and pins used by the application, and those pins match a UART mapping supported by the board.
criteria.observable: Selected board configuration's UART instance and pin assignments, compared with the board mapping
preconditions: A board configuration has been selected.
procedure: Inspect the selected board configuration for the UART instance and pin assignments used by the application.
Compare that instance and pin mapping with the supported mapping for the selected board.
criteria.expected: The UART instance and pins are identified and form a board-supported mapping.

criteria.criterion: After reset, clock and FPU initialization are complete before the application enters the test sequence.
criteria.observable: Target-side initialization state and test-sequence entry event
preconditions: The MCU has been reset.
procedure: Reset the MCU and run the application on the target.
Observe the clock and FPU initialization completion state and the test-sequence entry event.
criteria.expected: Clock and FPU initialization complete before test-sequence entry.

criteria.criterion: After reset, serial-console initialization completes before the application enters the test sequence.
criteria.observable: Target-side serial-console initialization state and test-sequence entry event
preconditions: The MCU has been reset.
procedure: Reset the MCU and run the application on the target.
Observe serial-console initialization completion and the test-sequence entry event.
criteria.expected: Serial-console initialization completes before test-sequence entry.

criteria.criterion: If clock, FPU, or serial-console initialization fails, the target run reports test failure and does not proceed into the test sequence.
criteria.observable: Target test status and test-sequence entry state under an injected initialization failure
preconditions: The target test can induce or simulate an initialization failure.
procedure: Induce each initialization failure supported by the test setup.
Observe the reported test status and whether the test sequence is entered.
criteria.expected: The run reports failure and does not enter the test sequence.
criteria.rationale: The requirement's failure behavior explicitly says any initialization failure shall fail the test; checking the failure status and blocked sequence is the observable consequence of that behavior.

criteria.criterion: After firmware flashing and a hardware reset, the ST-LINK Virtual COM Port receives startup output and the application reaches its execution-start state.
criteria.observable: ST-LINK Virtual COM Port output and application execution-start state
preconditions: The firmware has been flashed to the board.
The ST-LINK Virtual COM Port is connected to a capture host.
procedure: Apply a hardware reset to the board.
Capture the Virtual COM Port output.
Observe whether the application reaches its execution-start state.
criteria.expected: Startup output is present after reset and the application reaches its execution-start state.

criteria.criterion: Firmware flashes to a physical NUCLEO-C5A3ZG and, after hardware reset, produces startup output and begins application execution.
criteria.observable: ST-LINK flashing result, startup output, and application execution-start state
preconditions: A physical NUCLEO-C5A3ZG board and ST-LINK connection are available.
A successful firmware build is available.
procedure: Flash the firmware to the physical board using ST-LINK.
Apply a hardware reset.
Capture startup output and observe whether application execution begins.
criteria.expected: Flashing completes, startup output is present after reset, and application execution begins.

criteria.criterion: The target execution trace records clock and FPU initialization completion before ML runtime initialization and before the first inference call.
criteria.observable: Target-side ordered initialization and inference trace
preconditions: The MCU has been reset.
Target instrumentation records the relevant initialization and inference events.
procedure: Run the instrumented application on the target.
Read the event trace through the first inference call.
Compare the event ordering.
criteria.expected: Clock and FPU initialization complete before ML runtime initialization, and both complete before the first inference call.

criteria.criterion: If required clock or FPU initialization fails, the target run fails without entering ML runtime initialization or executing inference.
criteria.observable: Target failure status and ML-runtime/inference event trace after an induced initialization failure
preconditions: The target test can induce or simulate clock or FPU initialization failure.
procedure: Induce a required clock or FPU initialization failure.
Run the application and inspect its status and event trace.
criteria.expected: The run reports failure, with no ML runtime initialization or inference event after the failure.

criteria.criterion: Repeated hardware resets produce identical initial test-status, vector-counter, and comparison-result state before the first vector executes.
criteria.observable: Target RAM snapshot of test status, vector counters, and comparison results immediately before first-vector execution
preconditions: The application is running on the target.
The test can capture the listed state before the first vector execution.
procedure: Capture the listed state immediately before the first vector on one run.
Hardware-reset the board and capture the same state at the same point on a second run.
Compare the snapshots.
criteria.expected: The initial snapshots are identical across the two runs.

criteria.criterion: Under identical execution conditions, repeated hardware-reset runs produce the same vector count, comparison results, and final PASS/FAIL status.
criteria.observable: Target-reported vector count, comparison results, and final status for each run
preconditions: The same test inputs and execution conditions can be applied to repeated runs.
procedure: Run the test and record its vector count, comparison results, and final status.
Hardware-reset the board and repeat under identical execution conditions.
Compare the recorded results.
criteria.expected: Vector count, comparison results, and final PASS/FAIL status match between runs.

criteria.criterion: The test-state initialization event occurs before the first vector execution, and a run with stale or indeterminate initial state cannot report PASS.
criteria.observable: Target event ordering and final test status when stale or indeterminate state is introduced
preconditions: The target test can observe initialization and vector-execution events.
The test setup can introduce or simulate stale or indeterminate state.
procedure: Observe initialization and first-vector event ordering during a normal run.
Introduce or simulate stale or indeterminate test state before a run.
Observe whether the run reports PASS.
criteria.expected: Initialization precedes the first vector; the stale-state run does not report PASS.

criteria.criterion: The captured ST-LINK VCP log contains a result for each of the five specified vector comparisons.
criteria.observable: Captured ST-LINK VCP log
preconditions: The firmware is running on the NUCLEO-C5A3ZG after reset.
procedure: Capture the complete VCP output for one run.
Check the log for a result corresponding to each of the five specified vectors.
criteria.expected: 5 vector comparison results, one for each specified vector.

criteria.criterion: Repeated reset runs with the same firmware and model produce byte-identical result output containing a PASS or FAIL status.
criteria.observable: Captured result output from repeated reset runs
preconditions: The same firmware and model are deployed for all runs.
The board can be reset between runs.
procedure: Capture the result output after a reset.
Reset the board and capture the result output again.
Compare the result output bytes and check that a PASS or FAIL status is present.
criteria.expected: The result output is byte-identical across runs and contains a PASS or FAIL status.

criteria.criterion: The result output is concise.
criteria.expected: No pass condition can be stated because no maximum length or other definition of “concise” is specified.
criteria.rationale: The statement requires concision but supplies no length limit or definition that would distinguish a passing result from a failing one.
criteria.blocked_reason: A maximum output length or objective definition of “concise” is missing.

criteria.criterion: The UART signal to the ST-LINK VCP uses 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, and no flow control.
criteria.observable: UART configuration and framing on the ST-LINK VCP connection
preconditions: The NUCLEO-C5A3ZG is powered and the ST-LINK VCP connection is available.
procedure: Run the firmware.
Inspect the UART framing with a serial analyzer or equivalent instrument.
criteria.expected: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, and no flow control.

criteria.criterion: A VCP receiver configured for 115200 baud and 8-N-1 without flow control captures the firmware's console output without framing errors.
criteria.observable: Captured console output and receiver framing-error indication
preconditions: The firmware is running on the board.
The VCP receiver is configured for 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, and no flow control.
procedure: Connect the configured receiver to the ST-LINK VCP.
Capture a complete firmware run.
Check that output is received and the receiver reports no framing errors.
criteria.expected: Console output is received and the receiver reports zero framing errors.

criteria.criterion: A successful run produces exactly five vector result lines and one final summary line in the console log.
criteria.observable: Captured ST-LINK VCP log
preconditions: The firmware is running with all five reference vectors available.
procedure: Capture the complete console output for a run.
Count the vector result lines and final summary lines.
criteria.expected: Exactly 5 vector result lines and exactly 1 final summary line.

criteria.criterion: A console transmission failure during the run causes the test result to fail rather than pass.
criteria.observable: Captured final status and test result
preconditions: A test setup can force a console transmission failure.
procedure: Force a console transmission failure during a required result transmission.
Capture any subsequent console output and inspect the final test status.
criteria.expected: The test status is FAIL; it is not reported as PASS.

criteria.criterion: An injected vector or runtime failure produces a final FAIL status and a log entry identifying the failing condition when subsequent console output is available.
criteria.observable: Captured ST-LINK VCP log and final status
preconditions: The test setup can inject a vector or runtime failure.
Console output remains available after the injected failure.
procedure: Inject a vector failure and capture the console output.
Repeat with a runtime-operation failure.
Check each log for the failure condition and final status.
criteria.expected: Each run reports the injected failing condition and ends with status FAIL.

criteria.criterion: Each displayed output value is an integer equal to the corresponding comparison output multiplied by 1000.
criteria.observable: Parsed integer output values in the captured console log
preconditions: Output comparisons have completed.
The corresponding unscaled output values are available to the test.
procedure: Capture the output values printed for the comparisons.
For each value, multiply its corresponding unscaled output by 1000.
Compare the result with the printed integer and check that the printed representation is an integer.
criteria.expected: For every displayed output, printed integer = corresponding output × 1000.

criteria.criterion: The startup console output contains the SHA-256 digest of the model deployed with the firmware.
criteria.observable: Model identifier in the captured startup log
preconditions: The model deployed with the firmware is available to compute or retrieve its SHA-256 digest.
procedure: Compute the SHA-256 digest of the deployed model.
Capture the startup console output after reset.
Check that the output contains the matching digest.
criteria.expected: The printed model identifier matches the SHA-256 digest of the deployed model.

criteria.criterion: ML_RUNTIME_READY appears after successful model and runtime initialization and is absent when either initialization fails.
criteria.observable: ML_RUNTIME_READY occurrences in the captured console log
preconditions: The test setup can exercise successful initialization and inject model or runtime initialization failures.
procedure: Run with successful model and runtime initialization and capture the log.
Inject a model initialization failure and capture the log.
Inject a runtime initialization failure and capture the log.
criteria.expected: The successful run contains ML_RUNTIME_READY after initialization; neither failure run contains ML_RUNTIME_READY.

criteria.criterion: The log contains exactly one ML_VECTOR result line for each executed vector and no ML_VECTOR result line for a vector that was not executed.
criteria.observable: ML_VECTOR lines in the captured console log
preconditions: The test setup can determine which vectors execute.
procedure: Capture the console log for a run.
Count the ML_VECTOR lines and associate each line with its executed vector.
criteria.expected: Each executed vector has exactly 1 ML_VECTOR line; each unexecuted vector has 0 such lines.

criteria.criterion: A simulated unsuccessful transmission of each required startup, vector-result, or final-status message sets the test result to FAIL and prevents a PASS summary.
criteria.observable: Application test-result state and summary text captured by the fake console transport
preconditions: The console transport is injectable or replaceable by a fake that can report a failed transmission.
The application flow can be run in a host unit test.
procedure: Configure the fake transport to fail one required startup message and check the test result and summary.
Repeat for a vector-result message and for a final-status message.
criteria.expected: For each injected failure, the test result is FAIL and no PASS summary is emitted.

criteria.criterion: Each named reference vector has exactly one ML_VECTOR line that identifies the vector and contains an explicit, parseable FP32 comparison outcome.
criteria.observable: ML_VECTOR lines in the captured console log
preconditions: The five reference vectors have been executed and compared.
procedure: Capture the console log.
For each of positive, first_clamped, second_clamped, zero_input, and both_clamped, locate its ML_VECTOR line.
Check that each line identifies one vector and contains a comparison outcome token that can be parsed.
criteria.expected: Exactly 1 identifiable ML_VECTOR line per named vector, each with an explicit parseable comparison outcome.

criteria.criterion: The captured serial log reports positive, first_clamped, second_clamped, zero_input, and both_clamped.
criteria.observable: Named vector results in the captured serial log
preconditions: The firmware is running after reset with the five test vectors enabled.
procedure: Capture the serial log for one run.
Check that a result for each of the five named vectors is present.
criteria.expected: A result is present for each of the 5 named vectors.

criteria.criterion: After all five vector comparisons and cleanup succeed, the final log contains exactly ML_SUMMARY passed=5 total=5 status=PASS.
criteria.observable: Final summary line in the captured console log
preconditions: All five reference vectors execute.
All five comparisons and cleanup succeed.
procedure: Run the firmware with all five comparisons and cleanup succeeding.
Capture the complete console output.
Check the final summary line for an exact match.
criteria.expected: The final summary is exactly `ML_SUMMARY passed=5 total=5 status=PASS`.

criteria.criterion: A failed vector, comparison, or cleanup operation prevents emission of a PASS summary.
criteria.observable: PASS summary occurrences in the captured console log
preconditions: The test setup can separately inject a vector, comparison, or cleanup failure.
procedure: Run separate cases injecting each of the three failure types.
Capture the console output for each case.
Check each log for a PASS summary.
criteria.expected: Zero PASS summaries are emitted in every failure case.

criteria.criterion: The startup and test-sequence call paths contain no dynamic heap allocation or reachable allocator calls.
criteria.observable: Source and call-graph audit for the complete test sequence, including calls to heap-allocation APIs
preconditions: The complete startup and test-sequence source is available.
procedure: Trace the startup and test-sequence call paths, including calls into linked libraries.
Check whether any path used during the sequence performs dynamic heap allocation.
criteria.expected: No dynamic heap allocation occurs on any startup or test-sequence path.

criteria.criterion: The build configuration and component artifacts identify the same Cortex-M33 CPU/FPU ABI for generated model sources, runtime libraries, and application objects.
criteria.observable: Compiler and linker ABI options and CPU/FPU attributes in the component objects and libraries
preconditions: Build configuration and generated model, runtime, and application artifacts are available.
procedure: Inspect the CPU/FPU ABI options used to build each component.
Inspect the ABI attributes recorded in the component artifacts.
Compare the CPU and FPU ABI settings across all listed components.
criteria.expected: All listed components use mutually compatible Cortex-M33 CPU/FPU ABI settings.

criteria.criterion: The final link produces a firmware artifact without unresolved symbols, ABI mismatch diagnostics, or overlapping memory-region diagnostics.
criteria.observable: Final linker output and linked firmware artifact
preconditions: The firmware build and link have been performed.
procedure: Inspect the final linker output for unresolved-symbol, ABI-mismatch, and overlapping-memory-region diagnostics.
Confirm that the linked firmware artifact was produced.
criteria.expected: A linked firmware artifact is present, with zero diagnostics for the three listed link conditions.

criteria.criterion: The linker map places all Flash sections within 1 MiB and all SRAM sections within 256 KiB of the target memory regions.
criteria.observable: Linker map section addresses, sizes, and target memory-region bounds
preconditions: The firmware has linked and its linker map is available.
procedure: Read the Flash and SRAM region bounds from the linker map.
Check each placed section's address range against its assigned region.
criteria.expected: Placed Flash sections remain within 1 MiB, and placed SRAM sections remain within 256 KiB.

criteria.criterion: A complete build configured for NUCLEO-C5A3ZG produces a successfully linked firmware artifact.
criteria.observable: Build result and final firmware artifact for NUCLEO-C5A3ZG
preconditions: Complete application source and model are available.
procedure: Run the complete firmware build configured for NUCLEO-C5A3ZG.
Inspect the build result and confirm the final firmware artifact was produced.
criteria.expected: The build and link succeed for NUCLEO-C5A3ZG, and the target firmware artifact is present.

criteria.criterion: Two fresh builds from identical source and model inputs produce equivalent startup, five-vector, and final-summary behavior when run on the target board.
criteria.observable: Serial-console logs from the two target-board runs
preconditions: The two builds use identical source and model inputs.
The target board and ST-LINK Virtual COM Port are available.
procedure: Create two fresh firmware builds from the identical source and model inputs.
Run each build on the same target board and capture its serial-console output.
Compare the startup output, all five vector results, and the final summary between the captures.
criteria.expected: The two captures show equivalent startup behavior, the same five vector results, and equivalent final-summary behavior.

criteria.criterion: The delivered package contains the STM32 project source required to build the application.
criteria.observable: Delivered package file tree and STM32 project source files
preconditions: The delivery package is available for review.
procedure: Inspect the delivered package file tree.
Confirm it contains the STM32 project source needed for the application build.
criteria.expected: STM32 project source required to build the application is present in the delivered package.

criteria.criterion: The delivered package contains a final firmware binary or ELF artifact for the target board.
criteria.observable: Delivered package file tree and firmware binary/ELF artifact
preconditions: A successful firmware build has been performed.
The delivery package is available for review.
procedure: Inspect the delivered package file tree.
Confirm that it contains the final firmware binary or ELF artifact for the target board.
criteria.expected: At least one final firmware binary or ELF artifact for the target board is present in the package.

criteria.criterion: The delivered package contains a SHA-256 identifier that matches the deployed model.
criteria.observable: Delivered SHA-256 identifier and SHA-256 digest computed from the deployed model
preconditions: The deployed model and delivery package are available for review.
procedure: Read the SHA-256 identifier in the delivered package.
Compute the SHA-256 digest of the deployed model.
Compare the delivered identifier with the computed digest.
criteria.expected: The delivered identifier is a 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest and matches the deployed model's computed digest.
criteria.rationale: The stated acceptance criterion requires delivery of the model's SHA-256 identifier; comparing it with the deployed model's digest checks that the delivered identifier actually identifies that model rather than merely being present.

criteria.criterion: The delivered serial-log capture contains startup output, five vector-result lines, and a final PASS or FAIL summary.
criteria.observable: Delivered serial-log file
preconditions: The firmware has been executed on the target board.
The delivery package is available for review.
procedure: Open the delivered serial-log capture.
Check for startup output, count the vector-result lines, and inspect the final summary.
criteria.expected: The capture contains startup output, exactly five vector-result lines, and a final PASS or FAIL summary.

criteria.criterion: The delivered validation record identifies the board used, firmware build result, flash result, and observed inference result.
criteria.observable: Delivered validation record
preconditions: Validation has been performed.
The delivery package is available for review.
procedure: Open the delivered validation record.
Check for an entry identifying each of the board, build result, flash result, and observed inference result.
criteria.expected: All four required items are identified in the record.

criteria.criterion: The memory map and runtime-storage evidence account for stack, static, activation, context, and I/O storage within the target's 256 KiB SRAM allocation.
criteria.observable: Linker map and runtime-storage sizing evidence for the listed storage categories
preconditions: The final linked firmware and its memory map are available.
Runtime-storage sizes for stack, static, activation, context, and I/O storage are available.
procedure: Inspect the map and runtime-storage evidence for each listed storage category.
Check that the accounted storage fits within the target SRAM allocation without exceeding its bounds.
criteria.expected: All listed runtime storage is accounted for within 256 KiB (262144 bytes) of target SRAM.

criteria.criterion: During startup and execution of all five vectors, the stack high-water mark remains within its allocated stack range and the runtime stack-overflow indicator remains clear.
criteria.observable: Target runtime stack high-water mark and stack-overflow indicator
preconditions: The final firmware is running on the target MCU.
Runtime stack high-water and overflow evidence is available.
procedure: Run startup and the complete five-vector sequence on the target.
Read the stack high-water mark and stack-overflow indicator after the sequence.
criteria.expected: The measured stack use does not exceed the allocated stack size, and the stack-overflow indicator is clear.
criteria.rationale: The acceptance criterion requires worst-case sequence execution without stack overflow and calls for runtime evidence. Checking stack high-water use against its allocation and the overflow indicator provides observable evidence for that runtime condition.

criteria.criterion: The NUCLEO-C5A3ZG completes an inference by executing the supplied FP32 model on its MCU CPU.
criteria.observable: ST-LINK Virtual COM Port inference trace and the target-side model execution trace
preconditions: The firmware containing the supplied FP32 model is flashed to the NUCLEO-C5A3ZG.
procedure: Reset the board and capture the ST-LINK Virtual COM Port output and target-side execution trace.
Run the model inference and check that the trace records execution on the MCU CPU and completion.
criteria.expected: The trace records a completed model inference on the MCU CPU.

criteria.criterion: A comparison of the deployed model with c5_dense_relu.onnx finds no graph or weight changes.
criteria.observable: The source and deployed model graph and weight data
preconditions: The supplied model and deployed model artifact are available for inspection.
procedure: Compare the source and deployed model graphs.
Compare the corresponding model weight data.
criteria.expected: The graph and weights match without changes.

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the deployed ONNX artifact confirms FP32 tensors, opset 17, IR version 8, and exactly one input named input and one output named output, each with shape [1,2].
criteria.observable: The deployed ONNX model metadata, graph inputs, and graph outputs
preconditions: The deployed ONNX model artifact is available for inspection.
procedure: Read the model IR version and opset metadata.
Inspect the input and output tensor counts, names, element types, and shapes.
criteria.expected: IR version is 8; opset is 17; there is one FP32 input named input with shape [1,2] and one FP32 output named output with shape [1,2].

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the deployed model graph finds MatMul, Add, and Relu as its operations and finds no other operation types.
criteria.observable: The deployed ONNX graph's node operation types
preconditions: The deployed ONNX model artifact is available for inspection.
procedure: Enumerate the operation type of each node in the deployed model graph.
Compare the resulting operation types with the required set.
criteria.expected: The graph operation types are MatMul, Add, and Relu only.

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the inference data path finds direct FP32 input and output handling and no additional preprocessing or postprocessing.
criteria.observable: The source code path from FP32 input delivery to FP32 output retrieval
preconditions: The inference implementation is available for source inspection.
procedure: Trace how input values are passed to the model.
Trace how output values are retrieved and returned.
Check those paths for transformations beyond direct FP32 handling.
criteria.expected: Input and output values are handled directly as FP32, with no additional preprocessing or postprocessing.

criteria.criterion: The inference execution trace shows inference dispatched through the compiled model using the ST AI runtime.
criteria.observable: The target-side inference trace identifying the compiled model and ST AI runtime call
preconditions: The firmware with the compiled model and ST AI runtime is flashed to the target.
procedure: Reset the target and capture its inference execution trace.
Run an inference and inspect the recorded dispatch path.
criteria.expected: The trace identifies an inference call through the ST AI runtime using the compiled model.

criteria.criterion: The inference call path invokes the compiled model's inference entry point rather than a handwritten implementation of the model equations.
criteria.observable: The source-level inference call path
preconditions: The inference implementation and generated model sources are available for inspection.
procedure: Trace the application inference call to its implementation.
Check whether that path invokes the compiled model or performs the model equations directly.
criteria.expected: The application inference path invokes the compiled model and does not substitute handwritten model equations.

criteria.criterion: After reset initialization, generated-network initialization succeeds and all required activation, context, and I/O buffers are available before the first inference.
criteria.observable: The target-side network initialization result, required buffer descriptors, and ordering relative to the first inference
preconditions: Reset initialization is complete.
The generated network's required activation, context, and I/O buffers are identified by its generated configuration.
procedure: Start the firmware on the target and observe generated-network initialization.
Check the initialization result and required buffer descriptors.
Confirm these checks occur before the first inference.
criteria.expected: Network initialization succeeds; every required buffer is available to the network before the first inference.

criteria.criterion: The ML runtime deinitialization operation is invoked after completion of the fifth vector execution.
criteria.observable: The target-side sequence of vector-completion and runtime-deinitialization events
preconditions: The test sequence executes all five vectors on the target.
procedure: Capture the target-side event trace for the five vector executions.
Check the position of the runtime deinitialization event in the trace.
criteria.expected: All five vector executions complete before the ML runtime deinitialization operation is invoked.

criteria.criterion: The build configuration and generated model artifacts identify STM32C5 CPU execution as the model target.
criteria.observable: The model-generation configuration and generated model target metadata
preconditions: The model-generation configuration and generated model artifacts are available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the model-generation target settings.
Inspect the generated model target metadata.
criteria.expected: Both identify STM32C5 CPU execution as the target.

criteria.criterion: The delivered runtime integration identifies an ST AI compatible C runtime for model execution.
criteria.observable: The runtime integration configuration and linked runtime component records
preconditions: The runtime integration configuration and build records are available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the runtime configuration used for model execution.
Inspect the build records for the runtime component used.
criteria.expected: The model execution runtime is identified as an ST AI compatible C runtime.

criteria.criterion: Comparison of the supplied ONNX model with the conversion inputs and outputs finds no changes to the model graph or weights.
criteria.observable: The supplied ONNX model and conversion artifacts
preconditions: The supplied ONNX model and conversion artifacts are available for inspection.
procedure: Compare the graph used for conversion with the supplied model graph.
Compare the corresponding weights.
criteria.expected: The graph and weights are unchanged from the supplied model.

criteria.criterion: The delivered conversion output contains inference code generated for deployment on STM32C5.
criteria.observable: The conversion output and its target metadata
preconditions: The conversion output is available for inspection.
procedure: Inspect the conversion output for generated inference code.
Inspect its target metadata.
criteria.expected: Inference code is present and the target metadata identifies STM32C5.

criteria.criterion: The delivered project package contains the compiled ML model sources and the runtime integration files required by its build configuration.
criteria.observable: The delivered package file list and project build configuration
preconditions: The delivered project package and its build configuration are available for inspection.
procedure: Identify the compiled model sources and runtime integration files required by the build configuration.
Check that each is present in the delivered package.
criteria.expected: All compiled ML model sources and runtime integration files required by the build configuration are present in the package.

criteria.criterion: Inspection of the firmware image and linked model data confirms that the model weights and biases required for inference are embedded in the image.

preconditions: The firmware source and model-loading implementation are available for inspection.
procedure: Trace how the inference path obtains model weights and biases.
Check whether the path requires reading model or weight data from external storage.
criteria.expected: Inference obtains the required model data from the firmware image and does not require external model or weight storage.

criteria.criterion: The SHA-256 identifier in the startup log matches an independently calculated SHA-256 of the model artifact embedded in the firmware and used by the ST AI runtime.

Calculate its SHA-256 independently.
Compare that value with the identifier in the startup log.
criteria.expected: The startup identifier exactly matches the independently calculated SHA-256 of the embedded model artifact used by the runtime.

criteria.criterion: A run records exactly one inference call for each of the five reference-vector IDs and records no other inference calls.

Run the reference-vector test once.
Inspect the complete inference-call trace.
criteria.expected: The trace contains exactly five calls, one for each reference-vector ID, with no duplicate or additional calls.

criteria.criterion: For each vector, the event trace records comparisons of both original FP32 outputs against their expected values before any display conversion or formatting event.

A vector inference has completed.
procedure: Run the test with event recording enabled.
Inspect the events for each vector in order.
criteria.expected: Each vector has two FP32 comparison events before its first display-conversion or formatting event; the full run contains ten comparison events.

criteria.criterion: Injecting each listed initialization, inference, non-finite-output, deinitialization, and console-transmission failure leaves the final test status at FAIL and does not set or report PASS.
criteria.observable: The application’s final status and pass-reported state after each injected failure.
preconditions: Each failure source can be injected through a replaceable interface or test hook.
The application’s final status remains inspectable even when console transmission fails.
procedure: Run the test once for each of the five failure sources, injecting that failure in its corresponding operation.
After each run, inspect the final status and whether PASS was reported.
criteria.expected: For every injected failure, final status is FAIL and PASS is not reported.

criteria.criterion: The FP32 comparator accepts an output whose absolute difference is within 0.000001 of the expected value and rejects one outside that bound, without adding relative-tolerance allowance.
criteria.observable: The comparator function’s return value for the supplied FP32 actual and expected values.
preconditions: The comparator function is callable in a host test.
procedure: Compare FP32 actual 1.0000009536743164 against expected 1.0.
Compare FP32 actual 1.0000010728836059 against expected 1.0.
Inspect the comparator result for each call.
criteria.expected: The first comparison passes and the second fails; the acceptance boundary is absolute error <= 0.000001 with relative tolerance 0.

criteria.criterion: A complete five-vector test run counts as passing only when all ten original FP32 output comparisons are within absolute tolerance 0.000001 with relative tolerance 0.
criteria.observable: The host test’s per-output comparison results and final vector/test pass states.
preconditions: The application comparison flow is callable in a host test.
The five reference vectors and their expected FP32 outputs are available to the test.
procedure: Run the comparison flow for all five vectors using outputs within the specified tolerance.
Repeat with one output outside the specified tolerance.
Inspect the ten comparison results and the affected vector’s pass state.
criteria.expected: With all outputs in tolerance, all ten comparisons pass; when any output is outside tolerance, its comparison and vector do not pass.

criteria.criterion: Injecting a wrong output, a missing output, a non-finite output, or an ML runtime failure produces an outcome other than PASS for each case.
criteria.observable: The application’s final test outcome after each injected condition.

procedure: Run one test for each of the four conditions: wrong output, missing output, non-finite output, and runtime failure.

criteria.expected: None of the four runs has final outcome PASS.

criteria.criterion: The test documentation identifies a fixed execution order containing each of the five reference vectors exactly once.
criteria.observable: The documented reference-vector execution sequence in the test documentation or source comments.
preconditions: The application source and its test documentation are available for review.
procedure: Locate the documented reference-vector execution sequence.
Check its entries and their order.
criteria.expected: One fixed sequence is stated, and it lists each of the five reference vectors exactly once.
criteria.rationale: The requirement explicitly calls for a documented order but does not provide the order itself; this checks that the order is actually specified without inventing which vector must come first.

criteria.criterion: Repeated target resets with the same firmware produce the five vector executions and result lines in the documented order on every run.
criteria.observable: The ordered vector-execution and result lines captured through the ST-LINK Virtual COM Port across reset runs.
preconditions: Application initialization succeeds on the NUCLEO-C5A3ZG.

procedure: Reset the target and capture the vector execution and result lines.
Repeat the reset and capture the lines again.
Compare each run’s order with the documented sequence and with the other run.
criteria.expected: Every captured run contains the five vectors once, in the documented order, and the ordered sequences are identical across runs.
